abstract: Cancer-like genetic variants threaten bioreactor expansion of human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) for cell therapy manufacturing. Simulating scale-up versus scale-out, we find batch size, not master stock size, governs variant risk. Scale-out compartmentalizes risk and detects contamination sooner but amplifies rare variants. With risk factored, scale-out lowers hPSC manufacturing cost. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.
